Hi all,  We have finished our GSOC for 2024 but are already looking forwards to hopefully participating and having some great new projects in GSOC 2025.  Its great to already see interest is gathering for this:chart_with_upwards_trend:.

For those that want to get ahead and understand more about Mifos and its projects to enhance their applications, or just contribute I would highly recommend signing up for one of our Monthly volunteering calls.  On these calls we give an overview of Mifos and its projects to help you identify where you may want to start.   Our next volunteering call is on the 10th December 3pm UTC.  To receive these details go to this page and click "sign up to be a volunteer":  <https://mifos.org/take-action/volunteer/>

As we will explain on the call some of the best ways to get started is join our slack channels - congratulations if you are reading this you already have done this step:white_check_mark:.  But also download the code :technologist:try installing it and get a feel for it.  All our code is in Github ready to download  and we also have Mifos Gazelle which eases installation and if you have issues the community can help you <#C0F5D59L3|> is a good place to start or we have more dedicated channels on specific areas you can join (any issues joining reach out to me).

Although we will list projects when GSOC opens up we are always interesting in community ideas for new projects so if you have a thought about a project we should consider next year please do let one of the Mifos team know and we can work with you to see how it might fit.

Hey everyone. During my journey to understand the flow of the *Fineract* project, I found the following videos which helped me to figure out multiple things, and found it useful to share, if it would help anyone.
• <https://youtu.be/8qp3zQGh5s4|Modularizing Fineract>
• <https://youtu.be/fn9uhpOWrHk|Monolith to Microservices: Modularizing Fineract 1.x>
• <https://youtu.be/sfp7ox3wMKk|Expanding Fineract capabilities>
*I took some bullet points here as a summary, but for sure the videos are much more valuable.*

• <@U5JRP3L6N>  is the release manager of Fineract and he contributes with frequent electricity outages (No excuses for you xD)
• After community growth and time passes, things get more complicated with monolithic architecture (`Loan.java` exceeded 7000 LOC)
    ◦ For that, the need for modularity and separation comes into the scene, check this <https://martinfowler.com/bliki/images/microservice-verdict/productivity.png|Picture>.
• The flow of the application goes as follows:
    ◦ Requests are sent from the client to the Fineract server.
    ◦ API layer (RESTful APIs developed with JAX-RS) receives the request
    ◦ When receiving PUT or POST requests the attached JSON is stored as a string blob and is converted manually with GSON library to Java POJO.
    ◦ A portion of the requests are translated into commands.
    ◦ The commands are related to CQRS pattern for separation between Reads & Writes. (e.g. `GLAccountReadPlatformService` and `GLAccountWritePlatformService`)
    ◦ The commands go to a spring injectable service for command processing (handler packages) which delegates the command to the service layer to be executed.
    ◦ The execution flow happens synchronously.
    ◦ Check this <https://github.com/apache/fineract/assets/87117386/d66494ec-41b2-467d-9ba3-4c6de7a4f2a0|image>
• The code structure consists of around 12 top-level categories listed <https://github.com/apache/fineract/assets/87117386/c11b5493-b0f4-4973-ab4b-dbe01e7c5e31|here>
• Identifiable patterns in the codebase:
    ◦ api => The API layer that receives the client requests and is implemented with JAX-RS, which exposes some end-points that the client communicates with.
    ◦ data => The *D*ata *T*ransfer *O*bjects which encapsulates the data and transports it among different parts of the application.
    ◦ domain => Contain entities that map between database tables and java classes and contain some legacy logic in some files :)
    ◦ serialization => responsible for de/serializing between JSON files and java POJOs 
    ◦ exception => hold the project custom exceptions.
    ◦ utility => some utility classes that contain some shared and reusable code.
    ◦ handler => delegate the commands to the suitable service.
    ◦ mapper => contains the mapper classes that are responsible for mapping between entities and DTOs.
    ◦ service => the service layer which applies the business logic.
Finally, I'd like to highlight that these insights are just personal effort, there's a high possibility of mistakes (any feedback would be very appreciated). For sure I strongly recommend referring to the videos and <https://fineract.apache.org/docs/current/|documentation> where you will find more info about the history and the challenges for scalability and consistency and how they have been tackled.

Special thanks to <@U5JP6FGS0> and <@U5JRP3L6N> for these wonderful sessions <3

attachments.title: #1979 Home screen redesign
attachments.text:
Deeply nested View Hierarchy is very bad for Ui Renderding  
If any change happens in any view, RenderThread has to traverse such a deeply nested tree  
This increases time take by a lot and causes frame drops.  
Flattening view Heirarchy makes the height of this tree lesser and hence traversing time decreases, the flatter the tree, the faster the traversal.

Fixes <https://github.com/openMF/mifos-mobile/issues/1971|#1971>

Please Add Screenshots If there are any UI changes.

Both the layouts, the one after refactor and the one before looks the same, with slight styling improvements but with a huge difference in Layout Design and Performance

So the old Layout looked like:  
<https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/64367926/225014010-e633c796-4da1-4dfb-8e8a-0a5f999ba31d.png|image>

And the new refactored Layout looks like:  
<https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/64367926/225015297-ad220a41-2b0b-427a-b22d-2b069265f4e5.png|image>

You can clearly see how much the View Hierarchy has improved, this will get us huge performance gain while rendering this screen.

<!channel> Hello students and contributors,

I hope you guys have gone through the <https://mifosforge.jira.com/wiki/spaces/RES/pages/3004891137/Google+Summer+of+Code+2022+Ideas|Mifos Project Ideas List for GSoC '22> and decided which project you will contribute to this summer. As the deadline to submit your proposals is just around the corner, by now, you should be finishing up your proposals and giving the final touches.

I apologize for posting this late but here are some general guidelines to follow:
1. Please put the name of your project as the heading.
2. We have created an application template <https://mifosforge.jira.com/wiki/spaces/RES/pages/4456638/Application+Template|here>. We encourage you to use the same but you are free to edit the template as you see fit.
3. You are not required to elaborate on each and every point mentioned in the project ideas list. Elaborate on the points that *YOU* think are relevant.
4. We want to see how well you have understood the requirements of the project and how confident you are in delivering it. We want to see whether you have clarity on implementing the items mentioned in the ideas list.
5. Please keep your timeline realistic. Don’t overpromise. We know the scope of some projects is really big and can spill over the summer but that’s okay. We want to see how well can you take into account all to keep things real.
6. Make sure there are absolutely no grammatical mistakes. If needed, run your proposal through Grammarly. They have a chrome plugin for this.
7. Make sure the formatting (font size of heading, content, etc.) is uniform throughout the proposal. Keep the font of content as 12, if possible.
8. Avoid using many colors. Keep it simple.
9. Get your proposals reviewed by our mentors or past GSoC students or anyone who is in Open Source.
You can send your proposal’s google doc link to me for review. My email is <mailto:chinmaykulkarni8@gmail.com|chinmaykulkarni8@gmail.com>. Subject: GSoC ’22 Proposal <Project Name>
Body: Your name, and proposal link.

For any more questions, feel free to post them here and one of our team members should get back to you.

All the best! Cheers!

*REQUEST FOR HELP: Update UI Screenshots in Mifos X User Manual* 

For any of our aspiring interns or any of volunteers or individuals looking to contribute we have a set of small but meaningful tasks that would be super helpful to the community and a good way of starting to familiarize yourself with the capabilities of Mifos X.

We are seeking volunteers to finalize updating of screenshots throughout our user manual to reflect the current web app UI as a good percentage of screenshots were updated but throughout the user manual there are still a number of screenshots from our legacy community app UI. This would involve the following:

1. Log into the demo instance that we’re populating with clean sample data
2. For the section you’re assigned, follow the steps in the user manual to reproduce the screenshots in the new UI. All the flows should be the same, just the screens are different and navigation slightly different. 
3. You would then take the screenshot and insert into the documentation in gitbook the updated screenshot. 
Multiple people could work on this in parallel on the various sections that still need updating.
